recipe.title: Warm orange and rhubarb compote with yoghurt
recipe.intro: Early January brings the first bright pink forced rhubarb and the sweetest Spanish oranges. Together they make a sharp, sunny breakfast for a grey morning.
steps: Finely grate the zest from one orange. Cut the peel and white pith off all three oranges, then slice them into rounds or segments over a bowl to catch the juice.
Put the rhubarb in a saucepan with the zest, the caught juice, honey, cinnamon and water. Cover and simmer gently for 5 to 7 minutes, until the rhubarb is soft but still holding its shape.
Meanwhile, toast the almonds and pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking now and then, until golden and smelling nutty. Tip onto the board and roughly chop the almonds.
Take the rhubarb off the heat and gently stir in the orange pieces so they warm through without breaking up.
Spoon the yoghurt into four bowls, top with the warm compote and its juices, and scatter over the nuts and seeds.
recipe.tip: Make a double batch of compote. It keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer, and is just as good cold.
